# Tools

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_docs.py from the tool list the server publishes. Do not edit by hand. -->

These are the tools a client sees, grouped by tool group, with every built-in group turned on.
Descriptions and parameters are exactly what the server publishes.

Turn a group off with `tools.disabled` (or `--disable GROUP`), turn on an opt-in group with
`tools.enabled` (or `--enable GROUP`), and remove single tools with `tools.disabled_tools`; see
[configuration.md](configuration.md#tool-groups). `dev-link tools DIR` lists the tools a given
configuration publishes.

78 tools in 13 groups.

| Group | On by default | Needs extra | Tools |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`system`](#system) | yes | - | 2 |
| [`files`](#files) | yes | - | 13 |
| [`search`](#search) | yes | - | 3 |
| [`shell`](#shell) | yes | - | 2 |
| [`processes`](#processes) | yes | - | 6 |
| [`code`](#code) | yes | `code` | 4 |
| [`project`](#project) | yes | - | 6 |
| [`http`](#http) | yes | - | 3 |
| [`data`](#data) | yes | - | 4 |
| [`checkpoints`](#checkpoints) | yes | - | 4 |
| [`tasks`](#tasks) | yes | - | 7 |
| [`docker`](#docker) | no | - | 9 |
| [`browser`](#browser) | yes | `browser` | 15 |

## system

Workspace and server information. On by default.

### `server_status`

Server health: background processes, tool calls and errors in the last 24 hours, and
free disk space on the workspace volume.

No parameters.

Returns structured output (`structuredContent`) as well as text.

### `workspace_info`

Describe the environment: workspace root, sandbox mode and network access, limits, and
installed toolchains with versions. Call this first in a new session.

No parameters.

Returns text only.

## files

Reading, writing, editing and organising files inside the workspace. On by default.

### `apply_patch`

Apply a unified diff with `git apply`, also outside git repos. Patch paths are relative to
the workspace root. Can create, delete and rename files; hunk line counts are recomputed, so
slightly wrong @@ headers still apply. Nothing changes if any hunk fails.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `patch` | string | yes | - | Unified diff (git diff or diff -u); may touch many files. |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | `false` | Only check that the patch applies; change nothing. |
| `strip` | integer (>= 0, <= 10) | no | `1` | Leading path components to drop (1 for a/ and b/ prefixes). |

Returns text only.

### `copy_path`

Copy a file or a whole directory tree, keeping timestamps and permissions. `dst` is the new
path itself. Symlinks inside a copied directory are copied as links. Fails if `dst` exists
unless overwrite=true.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | string | yes | - | File or directory to copy. |
| `dst` | string | yes | - | Full destination path (not a directory to copy into). |
| `overwrite` | boolean | no | `false` | Replace an existing destination. |

Returns text only.

### `delete_path`

Delete a file, symlink (the link only, never its target) or directory. A non-empty directory
needs recursive=true. The workspace root cannot be deleted. There is no undo outside
checkpoints or git.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | yes | - | File, directory or symlink to delete. |
| `recursive` | boolean | no | `false` | Required to delete a non-empty directory. |

Returns text only.

### `edit_file`

Replace an exact string in a file and return a unified diff. Fails when the text is not
found, or matches more than once and replace_all is false.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | yes | - | Relative to the workspace root. |
| `old_string` | string | yes | - | Exact text to replace, including whitespace and indentation. |
| `new_string` | string | yes | - | Replacement text. |
| `replace_all` | boolean | no | `false` | Replace every occurrence. |

Returns text only.

### `file_info`

Metadata for a path: type, size, modification time, permissions, MIME guess, whether it is
binary, line count for text files up to the read limit, entry count for directories, and
symlink target.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | yes | - | Relative to the workspace root. |

Returns structured output (`structuredContent`) as well as text.

### `list_dir`

List one directory: directories first, then files with sizes, and symlinks with their
targets. Use tree for a recursive view.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | no | `"."` | Relative to the workspace root. |
| `show_hidden` | boolean | no | `false` | Include entries whose names start with a dot. |

Returns text only.

### `make_dir`

Create a directory and any missing parents. Succeeds if it already exists.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | yes | - | Directory to create, relative to the workspace root. |

Returns text only.

### `move_path`

Move or rename a file, directory or symlink. `dst` is the new path itself. Missing parent
directories are created. Fails if `dst` exists unless overwrite=true. Symlinks are moved as
links.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | string | yes | - | File, directory or symlink to move. |
| `dst` | string | yes | - | Full destination path (not a directory to move into). |
| `overwrite` | boolean | no | `false` | Replace an existing destination. |

Returns text only.

### `multi_edit`

Apply several exact-string edits to one file, all or nothing: if any edit fails, the file
is left unchanged and the error names the edit. Returns a unified diff of the result.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | yes | - | Relative to the workspace root. |
| `edits` | list of `EditSpec` (1 or more items) | yes | - | Edits applied in order; each sees the previous result. |

`EditSpec` fields:

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `old_string` | string | yes | - | Exact text to find, including whitespace and indentation. |
| `new_string` | string | yes | - | Replacement text. |
| `replace_all` | boolean | no | `false` | Replace every occurrence instead of requiring exactly one. |

Returns text only.

### `read_file`

Read a text file as numbered lines (`cat -n` style) with the total line count. Output
stops at the output cap with the offset to continue from; lines over 2000 characters are
cut. PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP files up to the read limit are returned as images. Other
binary files are refused.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | yes | - | Relative to the workspace root. |
| `offset` | integer (>= 1) | no | `1` | First line to return (1-based). |
| `limit` | integer (>= 1, <= 100000) | no | `2000` | Maximum number of lines to return. |

Returns text only.

### `read_many_files`

Read several text files in one call, each as numbered lines under a `==> path <==` header.
A file that cannot be read gets an inline error and the rest are still returned. Files past
the output cap and images are skipped; use read_file for them.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `paths` | list of string (1 or more items, up to 100 items) | yes | - |  |
| `limit_per_file` | integer (>= 1, <= 100000) | no | `500` | Maximum lines per file. |

Returns text only.

### `tree`

Recursive directory listing. Generated and vendored directories (.git, node_modules, .venv,
__pycache__, dist, build, target, caches) are listed as skipped, symlinks are not followed,
and directories at max_depth end with '/ ...'.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | no | `"."` | Relative to the workspace root. |
| `max_depth` | integer (>= 1, <= 20) | no | `3` | How many directory levels to descend. |
| `max_entries` | integer (>= 1, <= 10000) | no | `500` | Stop after this many entries. |

Returns text only.

### `write_file`

Create a file or replace its whole content; use edit_file or multi_edit to change part of
a file. An existing file is replaced atomically and keeps its permissions.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | yes | - | Relative to the workspace root. |
| `content` | string | yes | - | Full new file content (UTF-8). Line endings are kept as given. |
| `create_dirs` | boolean | no | `true` | Create missing parent directories. |

Returns text only.

## search

Content and file-name search with ripgrep, plus search-and-replace across files. On by default.

### `find_files`

Find files by name or path glob (ripgrep --files). Respects .gitignore and skips hidden
files by default. Returns workspace-relative paths sorted alphabetically, capped at max_results.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pattern` | string | yes | - | Glob for file paths. Without '/', it matches file names at any depth ('*.py', 'Dockerfile*'); with '/', it matches workspace-relative paths ('src/**/test_*.py'). |
| `path` | string | no | `"."` | Directory to search, relative to the workspace root. |
| `max_results` | integer (>= 1, <= 5000) | no | `500` | Max paths to return. |
| `ignore_case` | boolean | no | `false` | Case-insensitive glob matching. |
| `include_hidden` | boolean | no | `false` | Also search hidden files and directories (dot-files). .git is always skipped. |
| `include_ignored` | boolean | no | `false` | Also search files excluded by .gitignore/.ignore (node_modules, build output...). |

Returns text only.

### `grep`

Search file contents with ripgrep, skipping .gitignore'd, hidden and binary files by
default. content mode groups matches by file as `line: text` (context lines `line- text`);
files mode lists paths; count mode prints `path: count`. Sorted by path and capped at
max_results; the footer says when more exist.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pattern` | string | yes | - | Rust regex (ripgrep syntax), or literal text with fixed_strings. |
| `path` | string | no | `"."` | File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. |
| `glob` | string or null | no | `null` | Only search files matching this glob, e.g. '*.py' or 'src/**/*.ts'; '!x' excludes. |
| `ignore_case` | boolean | no | `false` | Case-insensitive matching. |
| `fixed_strings` | boolean | no | `false` | Treat pattern as literal text, not a regex. |
| `context` | integer (>= 0, <= 20) | no | `0` | Lines of context before and after each match. |
| `output_mode` | one of `content`, `files`, `count` | no | `"content"` | content: matching lines; files: file paths only; count: matching lines per file. |
| `max_results` | integer (>= 1, <= 5000) | no | `200` | Max matching lines (content) or files (files/count). |
| `include_hidden` | boolean | no | `false` | Also search hidden files and directories (dot-files). .git is always skipped. |
| `include_ignored` | boolean | no | `false` | Also search files excluded by .gitignore/.ignore (node_modules, build output...). |

Returns text only.

### `replace_in_files`

Search and replace across files, showing a unified diff per changed file. Defaults to a
dry run; call again with dry_run=false to write. Skips .gitignore'd, hidden, binary, non-UTF-8
and oversized files. Patterns can span lines; use (?m) for per-line ^ and $. Each file is
replaced atomically.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pattern` | string | yes | - | Python regex (re module), or literal text when regex=false. |
| `replacement` | string | yes | - | Replacement text. With regex=true, \1 or \g<name> insert captured groups. |
| `glob` | string or null | no | `null` | Only touch files matching this glob, e.g. '*.py' or 'src/**/*.ts'. |
| `path` | string | no | `"."` | File or directory, relative to the workspace root. |
| `regex` | boolean | no | `true` | Treat pattern as a regex; false means literal text. |
| `ignore_case` | boolean | no | `false` | Case-insensitive matching. |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | `true` | Preview only. Set false to write the changes. |
| `include_hidden` | boolean | no | `false` | Also search hidden files and directories (dot-files). .git is always skipped. |
| `include_ignored` | boolean | no | `false` | Also search files excluded by .gitignore/.ignore (node_modules, build output...). |

Returns text only.

## shell

One-shot shell commands and code snippets, run inside the sandbox. On by default.

### `run_code`

Run a code snippet from the workspace root without writing a file. The code is passed
on stdin, so the program cannot read stdin. Returns the same result as run_command.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `language` | one of `python`, `node`, `bash`, `sh`, `ruby`, `perl`, `php` | yes | - |  |
| `code` | string | yes | - | Program source. |
| `timeout_s` | number (> 0) or null | no | `null` | Seconds before the program is killed. Default 120, max 3600. |
| `args` | list of string or null | no | `null` | Command-line arguments for the program (sys.argv[1:], $1...). |

Returns text only.

### `run_command`

Run a shell command and wait for it to finish. Returns the exit code, duration, stdout
and stderr; a non-zero exit is reported in the text, not as a tool error. Use start_process
for servers, watchers and anything long-running: background jobs (`cmd &`, nohup) are
killed when the command returns. Sandboxed commands share a /tmp (emptied when
the server starts) and a private HOME, both kept between calls.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `command` | string | yes | - | Run with `bash -c`, so pipes, && and globs work. |
| `cwd` | string | no | `"."` | Working directory, relative to the workspace root. |
| `timeout_s` | number (> 0) or null | no | `null` | Seconds before the command is killed. Default 120, max 3600. |
| `env` | mapping of string to string or null | no | `null` | Extra environment variables. |
| `stdin` | string or null | no | `null` | Text sent to standard input. |

Returns text only.

## processes

Background processes: dev servers, watchers, REPLs and other long-running commands. On by default.

### `list_processes`

List background processes, running and exited, with id, name, command, cwd, pid,
status, uptime and log size. Only the 50 most recently exited processes are kept.

No parameters.

Returns structured output (`structuredContent`) as well as text.

### `process_input`

Write text to a running background process's stdin (answer a prompt, drive a REPL).
Read the reply with process_output. Refused while the process has more than
1 MiB of earlier input still unread.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | - | Process id from start_process. |
| `text` | string | yes | - | Text written to the process's stdin. |
| `newline` | boolean | no | `true` | Append a newline, like pressing Enter. |

Returns text only.

### `process_output`

Read a background process's combined stdout and stderr, with next_offset for the next
call. Each call returns at most the output cap and says when more remains.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | - | Process id from start_process, e.g. 'p1'. |
| `offset` | integer (>= 0) | no | `0` | Byte offset to read from; pass the previous next_offset to get only new output. |
| `tail_lines` | integer (>= 1) or null | no | `null` | Return only the last N lines instead of reading from offset. |

Returns text only.

### `start_process`

Start a long-running command (dev server, watcher, REPL) as a background process,
sandboxed like run_command, and return its id and the output so far. Can first wait for a
regex in the output or an open port; a wait timeout is reported, not raised, and the
process keeps running. Background processes are killed
when the server stops.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `command` | string | yes | - | Shell command run with bash -c, e.g. 'npm run dev'. |
| `name` | string or null | no | `null` | Short label shown in list_processes. |
| `cwd` | string | no | `"."` | Working directory, relative to the workspace root. |
| `env` | mapping of string to string or null | no | `null` | Extra environment variables. |
| `wait_for_pattern` | string or null | no | `null` | Regex; return once the output matches it (e.g. 'listening on'). |
| `wait_for_port` | integer or null | no | `null` | Return once this TCP port accepts connections on 127.0.0.1 or ::1. |
| `wait_timeout_s` | number (> 0) | no | `30.0` | Max seconds to wait for the pattern or port. |

Returns text only.

### `stop_process`

Stop a background process and everything it started: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 5s.
Returns the exit code and the last 20 lines of output. Safe to call on an exited process.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | - | Process id from start_process. |

Returns text only.

### `wait_for_process`

Wait until a background process's output matches a regex, a port accepts connections,
or the process exits, whichever comes first. Fails on timeout; the process keeps running.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | - | Process id from start_process. |
| `pattern` | string or null | no | `null` | Regex to wait for in the output. |
| `port` | integer or null | no | `null` | TCP port to wait for on 127.0.0.1 or ::1. |
| `timeout_s` | number (> 0) | no | `30.0` | Max seconds to wait. |

Returns text only.

## code

Code intelligence: outlines, symbol definitions, references and line statistics. On by default. Needs the `code` extra: `pip install 'dev-link-mcp[code]'`.

### `code_outline`

List the classes, functions, methods, interfaces, structs, enums and types declared in one
source file, nested by containment, with 1-based line ranges (`L12-40`). Parsed with
tree-sitter, which covers most languages; the reply says when a file's language is not one.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | yes | - | Source file, relative to the workspace root |

Returns text only.

### `code_stats`

Count files and total/code/comment/blank lines per language, like cloc. Skips .gitignore'd
and hidden files and vendor/build dirs (node_modules, .venv, dist, target, ...). Unrecognized,
binary and oversized files are counted under `skipped`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | no | `"."` | Directory or file, relative to the workspace root |

Returns structured output (`structuredContent`) as well as text.

### `find_references`

Find every line that mentions an identifier as a whole word (definitions, calls, imports,
comments), grouped by file with line numbers. A text match, not semantic; skips .gitignore'd
files and vendor/build dirs. Long lines are cut to 300 characters.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes | - | Identifier to look for, matched as a whole word |
| `path` | string | no | `"."` | File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root |
| `ignore_case` | boolean | no | `false` | Case-insensitive match |
| `max_results` | integer (>= 1, <= 5000) | no | `200` | Maximum matching lines to show |

Returns text only.

### `find_symbol`

Find where a symbol is defined (class, function, method, type, ...), not where it is used.
Files that mention the name, minus .gitignore'd and vendor/build dirs, are parsed with
tree-sitter. Returns `path:start-end kind name (in Parent)` lines.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes | - | Exact symbol name, e.g. `UserService` or `parse_args` |
| `path` | string | no | `"."` | File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root |
| `kind` | one of `class`, `function`, `method`, `interface`, `struct`, `enum`, `trait`, `impl`, `module`, `namespace`, `type` or null | no | `null` | Only definitions of this kind; `function` also matches methods |
| `max_results` | integer (>= 1, <= 1000) | no | `50` | Maximum definitions to return |

Returns text only.

## project

Project detection and the standard install/test/lint/format/build commands. On by default.

### `install_deps`

Install dependencies with the detected command (npm install, uv sync, go mod download,
cargo fetch, mvn install, bundle install, ...) or `command`. Returns the command, exit code
and output.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | no | `"."` | Project directory, relative to the workspace root. |
| `command` | string or null | no | `null` | Shell command to run instead of the detected install command. |
| `timeout_s` | number (> 0) | no | `600.0` | Seconds before the command is killed. Default 600, max 3600. |

Returns text only.

### `project_detect`

Inspect a project directory without running anything: languages, manifests, package
managers, frameworks, package.json scripts, Makefile targets, just recipes, compose
services, subprojects and the detected commands. `commands` holds the one per kind that
the run_* tools and install_deps use (Makefile/justfile first); `commands_by_manifest`
lists every candidate.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | no | `"."` | Project directory, relative to the workspace root. |

Returns structured output (`structuredContent`) as well as text.

### `run_build`

Build the project with the detected command (npm run build, go build ./..., cargo
build, mvn package, uv build, make build, ...) or `command`. Returns the command, exit
code and output.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | no | `"."` | Project directory, relative to the workspace root. |
| `command` | string or null | no | `null` | Shell command to run instead of the detected build command. |
| `timeout_s` | number (> 0) | no | `600.0` | Seconds before the command is killed. Default 600, max 3600. |

Returns text only.

### `run_format`

Run the formatter with the detected command (ruff format, black, prettier, gofmt, cargo
fmt, ...) or `command`. Rewrites files unless check is set. Returns the command, exit code
and output.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | no | `"."` | Project directory, relative to the workspace root. |
| `command` | string or null | no | `null` | Shell command to run instead of the detected format command. |
| `check` | boolean | no | `false` | Only report files that need formatting; do not change them. |
| `timeout_s` | number (> 0) or null | no | `null` | Seconds before the command is killed. Default 120, max 3600. |

Returns text only.

### `run_lint`

Run the linter with the detected command (ruff, eslint, go vet, clippy, rubocop, a
Makefile or package.json lint target, ...) or `command`. Returns the command, exit code
and output.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | no | `"."` | Project directory, relative to the workspace root. |
| `command` | string or null | no | `null` | Shell command to run instead of the detected lint command. |
| `fix` | boolean | no | `false` | Run the linter's auto-fix variant (edits files). |
| `timeout_s` | number (> 0) or null | no | `null` | Seconds before the command is killed. Default 120, max 3600. |

Returns text only.

### `run_tests`

Run the tests with the detected command or `command`. Fresh JUnit XML reports, or the
output of pytest, jest, vitest, mocha, go test, cargo, maven, gradle, dotnet, rspec, phpunit
or unittest, become passed/failed/skipped counts and a failures list of {name, message};
counts are null when no format is recognized. The raw output is always included. Failing
tests are a normal result, not a tool error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | no | `"."` | Project directory, relative to the workspace root. |
| `command` | string or null | no | `null` | Shell command to run instead of the detected test command. |
| `target` | string or null | no | `null` | One test file, directory, package or name to run (e.g. tests/test_api.py::test_x, ./pkg/..., com.acme.AppTest). Inserted into the detected command, or appended to `command`. |
| `timeout_s` | number (> 0) | no | `600.0` | Seconds before the command is killed. Default 600, max 3600. |

Returns structured output (`structuredContent`) as well as text.

## http

HTTP client tools: raw requests, readable page fetches, and downloads into the workspace. On by default.

### `download_file`

Download a URL into a workspace file, following redirects, creating parent directories
and overwriting an existing file. Nothing is written unless the response is 2xx and within
max_bytes. Returns the saved path, size, content type and sha256.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | string | yes | - | Absolute http:// or https:// URL to download. |
| `path` | string | yes | - | Destination file in the workspace. An existing directory gets the URL's file name. |
| `max_bytes` | integer (> 0) | no | `100000000` | Abort if the download is larger than this many bytes. |
| `timeout_s` | number or null | no | `null` | Total timeout in seconds. Default 30, max 3600. |

Returns text only.

### `fetch_url`

GET a URL and return its readable content: HTML as markdown-style text without scripts,
styles and navigation, JSON pretty-printed, other text as is. Long pages are clipped. Fails
on 4xx/5xx and on binary content (use download_file for that).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | string | yes | - | Absolute http:// or https:// URL of a page or document. |
| `timeout_s` | number or null | no | `null` | Total timeout in seconds. Default 30, max 3600. |

Returns text only.

### `http_request`

Send an HTTP request from the server process, not the sandbox, and return the status,
request headers (credentials redacted), response headers and body. JSON is pretty-printed,
binary bodies are summarized and long bodies are clipped; use download_file for the whole
body. 4xx/5xx responses are normal results.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | string | yes | - | Absolute http:// or https:// URL. |
| `method` | one of `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS` | no | `"GET"` | HTTP method. |
| `headers` | mapping of string to string or null | no | `null` | Request headers. |
| `body` | string or null | no | `null` | Raw request body. Do not combine with json. |
| `json` | any | no | `null` | Value sent as a JSON body with Content-Type application/json. |
| `timeout_s` | number or null | no | `null` | Total timeout in seconds. Default 30, max 3600. |
| `follow_redirects` | boolean | no | `true` | Follow 3xx redirects (up to 10). |

Returns text only.

## data

SQLite, JSON and CSV inspection tools. On by default.

### `csv_preview`

Summarize a delimited text file: delimiter, row count, each column's inferred type
(integer, float, boolean, date, datetime, string) and null count, then the first rows as
a table. Empty, NA, N/A, null, None and NaN count as null. Statistics cover up to the
first 100000 rows (fewer for very wide files: about 2 million cells).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | yes | - | CSV/TSV file, relative to the workspace root |
| `rows` | integer (>= 0, <= 1000) | no | `20` | Data rows to show (0 for the summary only) |
| `delimiter` | string or null | no | `null` | Field separator, e.g. ',', ';', '\|' or '\t'. Detected when omitted |
| `has_header` | boolean | no | `true` | Treat the first row as column names |

Returns text only.

### `json_query`

Run a jq filter over a JSON file and return jq's output. Use it to pull fields out of
large JSON files instead of reading them whole. Output is clipped at the output cap.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | yes | - | JSON or JSON Lines file, relative to the workspace root |
| `expression` | string | no | `"."` | jq filter, for example '.items[] \| {id, name}' |
| `raw_output` | boolean | no | `false` | Print strings without quotes (jq -r) |

Returns text only.

### `sqlite_query`

Run one SQL statement against a SQLite file and return a text table with the row count.
The database opens read-only unless write=true, which commits the statement and creates a
missing file. ATTACH and VACUUM INTO are blocked.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `db_path` | string | yes | - | SQLite database file, relative to the workspace root |
| `sql` | string | yes | - | One SQL statement. Use ? or :name placeholders for params. |
| `params` | list or object or null | no | `null` | Values for ? placeholders (list) or :name placeholders (object) |
| `max_rows` | integer (>= 1, <= 10000) | no | `200` | Rows to return; the rest are counted |
| `write` | boolean | no | `false` | Open read-write and commit. Needed for INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL; creates the file |
| `timeout_s` | number or null | no | `null` | Statement time limit in seconds; same default and maximum as run_command |

Returns text only.

### `sqlite_schema`

List every table and view in a SQLite file with its columns (type, NOT NULL, default,
primary key), plus the CREATE statements for indexes and triggers. Read-only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `db_path` | string | yes | - | SQLite database file, relative to the workspace root |

Returns text only.

## checkpoints

Workspace snapshots in a shadow git repository the agent cannot see. On by default.

### `checkpoint_create`

Snapshot the workspace files into a private checkpoint store, separate from the project's
git history. Skips .gitignore'd files, dependency/build dirs (node_modules, .venv, dist, build,
target, ...) and nested git repositories. Returns the checkpoint id, a summary of changes since
the previous one, and `not_snapshotted` errors for unreadable files.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | string | no | `""` | Short label for this snapshot, e.g. 'before refactor' |

Returns structured output (`structuredContent`) as well as text.

### `checkpoint_diff`

Show how the current workspace files differ from a checkpoint, as a unified diff
('-' lines are the checkpoint, '+' lines are now), including files created or deleted since.
Clipped at the output cap; narrow it with `path` or stat_only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | - | Checkpoint id from checkpoint_list |
| `path` | string or null | no | `null` | Limit the diff to this file or directory |
| `stat_only` | boolean | no | `false` | Only list changed files with line counts |

Returns text only.

### `checkpoint_list`

List checkpoints, newest first, with id, date and message. Each restore adds an automatic
'auto: before restore' checkpoint.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `max_count` | integer (>= 1, <= 1000) | no | `50` | Most recent checkpoints to return |

Returns structured output (`structuredContent`) as well as text.

### `checkpoint_restore`

Return workspace files to their state at a checkpoint: overwrites changed files, recreates
deleted ones and deletes files created since. Ignored files and dependency/build dirs are left
alone; checkpoint files they now block are listed in `not_restored`. An automatic checkpoint is
taken first, so restoring `auto_checkpoint` undoes the restore.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | - | Checkpoint id from checkpoint_list |
| `paths` | list of string or null | no | `null` | Restore only these files or directories; omit to restore the whole workspace |

Returns structured output (`structuredContent`) as well as text.

## tasks

Persistent task list and notes for long agent jobs. On by default.

### `note_delete`

Delete a named note permanently.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | string | yes | - | Note name. |

Returns text only.

### `note_list`

List saved notes with last-updated time (UTC) and size in bytes.

No parameters.

Returns text only.

### `note_read`

Return the full text of a named note.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | string | yes | - | Note name. |

Returns text only.

### `note_write`

Save a named note (findings, decisions, plans) that persists across sessions, replacing
any note with the same key. Notes larger than the output cap are rejected.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | string | yes | - | Note name, e.g. 'design' or 'findings/auth'. |
| `content` | string | yes | - | Full note text; replaces any existing note with this key. |

Returns text only.

### `task_add`

Add a task (status todo) to the task list, which persists across sessions and server
restarts. Use it to plan and track multi-step work. Returns the new task id.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | string | yes | - | Short task title (one line). |
| `details` | string | no | `""` | Optional longer description, acceptance criteria, etc. |
| `parent_id` | integer or null | no | `null` | Id of an existing task to nest this under. |

Returns text only.

### `task_list`

Show the task list with ids, statuses, details and progress notes. Without a filter, tasks
are shown as a tree (subtasks indented under parents); with a status filter, as a flat list.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | one of `todo`, `in_progress`, `done`, `blocked` or null | no | `null` | Only show tasks with this status. |

Returns text only.

### `task_update`

Change a task's status or title and/or append a timestamped progress note. Needs at
least one of status, notes, title.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | integer | yes | - | Task id from task_add or task_list. |
| `status` | one of `todo`, `in_progress`, `done`, `blocked` or null | no | `null` | New status. |
| `notes` | string or null | no | `null` | Progress note appended (with a timestamp) to the task's notes. |
| `title` | string or null | no | `null` | Replacement title. |

Returns text only.

## docker

Docker containers, images and compose projects through the host docker CLI. Opt-in: off unless `tools.enabled` lists it.

### `compose`

Run docker compose for a compose file in the workspace. The resolved config is refused, with
each problem listed, if it reaches outside the workspace (privileged, host namespaces, cap_add,
devices, external volumes, paths outside the workspace, unknown keys, ...) or its project name
belongs to containers from elsewhere. down keeps named volumes. Containers started with up or
restart are stopped (not removed) when the server stops. A failing command is a tool error
carrying compose's output.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | one of `up`, `down`, `ps`, `logs`, `build`, `restart` | yes | - | docker compose subcommand to run. |
| `file` | string or null | no | `null` | Compose file inside the workspace. Default: compose.yaml / docker-compose.yml in the workspace root. |
| `services` | list of string or null | no | `null` | Limit to these services. Default: all. |
| `detach` | boolean | no | `true` | For up: start in the background. False waits until the containers exit; on timeout compose is killed and the containers keep running (use down). |
| `tail` | integer (>= 1, <= 10000) | no | `200` | For logs: lines per service. |
| `timeout_s` | number (> 0) or null | no | `null` | Seconds before compose is killed. Default 600 (capped at 3600). |

Returns text only.

### `docker_build`

Build an image from a Dockerfile in the workspace; base images may be pulled. Returns the
build log (clipped); a failed build is a tool error carrying the log.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tag` | string | yes | - | Image tag to create, e.g. 'myapp:dev'. |
| `context` | string | no | `"."` | Build context directory, relative to the workspace root. |
| `dockerfile` | string or null | no | `null` | Dockerfile path inside the workspace. Default: <context>/Dockerfile. |
| `timeout_s` | number (> 0) or null | no | `null` | Seconds before the build is cancelled. Default 600 (capped at 3600). |

Returns text only.

### `docker_exec`

Run a shell command inside a running container started from this workspace. The image must
have `sh`. Returns exit code, stdout and stderr; a non-zero exit is reported in the text. On timeout
only the docker client is killed; the command may keep running in the container.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `container` | string | yes | - | Running container name or id started from this workspace. |
| `command` | string | yes | - | Shell command, run with `sh -c` inside the container. |
| `timeout_s` | number (> 0) or null | no | `null` | Seconds before the command is killed. Default 120, max 3600. |

Returns text only.

### `docker_images`

List local images with repository, tag, id, size and age.

No parameters.

Returns structured output (`structuredContent`) as well as text.

### `docker_logs`

Recent stdout and stderr of a container started from this workspace (docker_run or
compose), with timestamps.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `container` | string | yes | - | Container name or id started from this workspace. |
| `tail` | integer (>= 1, <= 10000) | no | `200` | Number of most recent lines. |

Returns text only.

### `docker_ps`

List host containers with id, name, image, state, status and ports. `workspace` is true
for containers started from this workspace; only those can be used with docker_logs,
docker_exec, docker_stop and docker_rm.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `all` | boolean | no | `false` | Include stopped containers. |

Returns structured output (`structuredContent`) as well as text.

### `docker_rm`

Remove a container started from this workspace. Fails on a running container unless
force is set. Named volumes are kept.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `container` | string | yes | - | Container name or id started from this workspace. |
| `force` | boolean | no | `false` | Kill and remove the container even if it is running. |

Returns text only.

### `docker_run`

Start a container labeled as belonging to this workspace, pulling the image if missing.
The workspace is the only host mount allowed; privileged mode and host namespaces are not
available. detach=True returns the container id and published ports; detach=False waits and
returns the exit code and output, like run_command, and removes the container. Detached
containers are stopped (not removed) when the server stops.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `image` | string | yes | - | Image to run, e.g. 'postgres:16' or a tag from docker_build. |
| `command` | list of string or null | no | `null` | Argv overriding the image CMD, e.g. ['sh', '-c', 'npm test']. Default: image CMD. |
| `name` | string or null | no | `null` | Container name. Default: generated by docker. |
| `ports` | list of string or null | no | `null` | Published ports: 'CONTAINER', 'HOST:CONTAINER' or 'IP:HOST:CONTAINER', optional '/udp'. Bound to 127.0.0.1 unless an IP is given. |
| `env` | mapping of string to string or null | no | `null` | Environment variables for the container. |
| `detach` | boolean | no | `true` | Run in the background and return the id. False waits for the container to exit. |
| `mount_workspace` | boolean | no | `true` | Bind-mount the workspace at /workspace (read-write) and start there. |
| `timeout_s` | number (> 0) or null | no | `null` | With detach=False: seconds before the container is killed and removed. Default 120, max 3600. |

Returns text only.

### `docker_stop`

Stop a running container started from this workspace with `docker stop`. The container is
kept; remove it with docker_rm.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `container` | string | yes | - | Container name or id started from this workspace. |

Returns text only.

## browser

Headless Chromium driven through Playwright for frontend work. On by default. Needs the `browser` extra: `pip install 'dev-link-mcp[browser]'`.

### `browser_click`

Click the first element matching the selector, waiting for it to be visible and enabled.
Returns the page url/title afterwards and console errors raised by the click. A click that starts
a navigation does not wait for it to finish; follow up with browser_wait if needed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page_id` | string | yes | - | Page id returned by browser_open (e.g. 'p1'). |
| `selector` | string | yes | - | Playwright selector: CSS ('#email', 'form button'), 'text=Sign in', or 'role=button[name="Save"]'. |
| `timeout_s` | number (> 0) | no | `15.0` | Seconds to wait before failing; capped at the server maximum. |

Returns structured output (`structuredContent`) as well as text.

### `browser_close`

Close a page and discard its recorded logs. Closing a page from browser_open also discards its
cookies and storage and closes the popups it opened; closing a popup closes only that popup.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page_id` | string | yes | - | Page id returned by browser_open (e.g. 'p1'). |

Returns text only.

### `browser_console`

Console messages (log, warning, error, ...) and uncaught page errors recorded since the page
opened or the last clear, oldest first, each with its source location.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page_id` | string | yes | - | Page id returned by browser_open (e.g. 'p1'). |
| `clear` | boolean | no | `false` | Forget the returned entries so the next call shows only new ones. |

Returns text only.

### `browser_eval`

Run JavaScript in the page and return the result as JSON. It runs with the page's privileges,
including its cookies, and can change page state. DOM nodes and other non-serializable values
come back as null or {}.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page_id` | string | yes | - | Page id returned by browser_open (e.g. 'p1'). |
| `script` | string | yes | - | JavaScript expression or function, e.g. 'document.title' or '() => [...document.querySelectorAll("li")].map(e => e.textContent)'. Promises are awaited. |
| `timeout_s` | number (> 0) | no | `15.0` | Seconds to wait before failing; capped at the server maximum. |

Returns text only.

### `browser_list_pages`

Open browser pages with their id, URL, title, viewport and number of console errors.

No parameters.

Returns structured output (`structuredContent`) as well as text.

### `browser_navigate`

Load a URL in an existing page, keeping its cookies and storage. Returns the new title,
HTTP status and console errors logged during the navigation.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page_id` | string | yes | - | Page id returned by browser_open (e.g. 'p1'). |
| `url` | string | yes | - | http(s) URL to load in this page. |
| `wait_until` | one of `load`, `domcontentloaded`, `networkidle`, `commit` | no | `"load"` | Load event to wait for before returning. |
| `timeout_s` | number (> 0) | no | `15.0` | Seconds to wait before failing; capped at the server maximum. |

Returns structured output (`structuredContent`) as well as text.

### `browser_network`

Network requests made by the page since it opened: method, URL, resource type, HTTP status,
failure reason and duration. By default only failures and >= 400 responses, newest last.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page_id` | string | yes | - | Page id returned by browser_open (e.g. 'p1'). |
| `failed_only` | boolean | no | `true` | Only requests that failed to complete or got an HTTP status >= 400. |
| `max_entries` | integer (>= 1, <= 1000) | no | `200` | Newest entries to return. |

Returns structured output (`structuredContent`) as well as text.

### `browser_open`

Open a new page in the shared Chromium and load a URL. Returns the page id used by the other
browser_* tools, plus title, HTTP status and console errors so far; console, page errors and
network requests are recorded from the start. Pages stay open until browser_close, or until the
browser closes after the server's idle timeout. browser_list_pages shows the page limit. Only
http(s) URLs; serve local files over HTTP with start_process.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | string | yes | - | http(s) URL to load, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:5173/, or about:blank. |
| `width` | integer (>= 200, <= 7680) | no | `1280` | Viewport width in CSS pixels. |
| `height` | integer (>= 200, <= 4320) | no | `800` | Viewport height in CSS pixels. |
| `device` | string or null | no | `null` | Emulate a Playwright device such as 'iPhone 13' or 'Pixel 7' (overrides width/height). |
| `wait_until` | one of `load`, `domcontentloaded`, `networkidle`, `commit` | no | `"load"` | Load event to wait for before returning. |
| `timeout_s` | number (> 0) | no | `15.0` | Seconds to wait before failing; capped at the server maximum. |

Returns structured output (`structuredContent`) as well as text.

### `browser_press`

Press a key or key chord on the page (or on a given element). Returns the page state and
console errors raised by the key press.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page_id` | string | yes | - | Page id returned by browser_open (e.g. 'p1'). |
| `key` | string | yes | - | Key or chord in Playwright syntax: 'Enter', 'Escape', 'Tab', 'ArrowDown', 'Control+a'. |
| `selector` | string or null | no | `null` | Focus this element first; default is the focused one. |
| `timeout_s` | number (> 0) | no | `15.0` | Seconds to wait before failing; capped at the server maximum. |

Returns structured output (`structuredContent`) as well as text.

### `browser_screenshot`

Take a PNG screenshot of an open page or of a URL. The image is returned inline and saved
under .dev-link/artifacts (git-ignored); the text part gives the saved workspace-relative path.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page_id` | string or null | no | `null` | Page to capture. Give this or url, not both. |
| `url` | string or null | no | `null` | Open this URL in a temporary page, capture it, and close it. |
| `selector` | string or null | no | `null` | Capture only the first element matching this. |
| `full_page` | boolean | no | `false` | Capture the whole scrollable page, not just the viewport. |
| `name` | string | no | `"screenshot"` | File name stem for the saved PNG. |
| `width` | integer (>= 200, <= 7680) | no | `1280` | Viewport width when url is used. |
| `height` | integer (>= 200, <= 4320) | no | `800` | Viewport height when url is used. |
| `timeout_s` | number (> 0) | no | `15.0` | Seconds to wait before failing; capped at the server maximum. |

Returns text only.

### `browser_select`

Choose an option in a <select> element by its value or label. Returns the selected values.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page_id` | string | yes | - | Page id returned by browser_open (e.g. 'p1'). |
| `selector` | string | yes | - | Playwright selector: CSS ('#email', 'form button'), 'text=Sign in', or 'role=button[name="Save"]'. |
| `value` | string | yes | - | Option value or visible label to select. |
| `timeout_s` | number (> 0) | no | `15.0` | Seconds to wait before failing; capped at the server maximum. |

Returns structured output (`structuredContent`) as well as text.

### `browser_set_viewport`

Resize the page viewport, e.g. to check responsive breakpoints. Media queries re-evaluate
immediately; the page is not reloaded.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page_id` | string | yes | - | Page id returned by browser_open (e.g. 'p1'). |
| `width` | integer (>= 200, <= 7680) | yes | - | Viewport width in CSS pixels. |
| `height` | integer (>= 200, <= 4320) | yes | - | Viewport height in CSS pixels. |

Returns structured output (`structuredContent`) as well as text.

### `browser_snapshot`

Readable outline of the page for deciding what to do next: title, URL, visible form fields,
buttons and links each with a selector usable in browser_click/browser_type, then the visible
text (clipped). Password values are never included.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page_id` | string | yes | - | Page id returned by browser_open (e.g. 'p1'). |

Returns text only.

### `browser_type`

Fill an input, textarea or contenteditable element with text, replacing what was there, and
fire input/change events. Set submit=True to press Enter afterwards. Use browser_press for
individual keys or shortcuts.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page_id` | string | yes | - | Page id returned by browser_open (e.g. 'p1'). |
| `selector` | string | yes | - | Playwright selector: CSS ('#email', 'form button'), 'text=Sign in', or 'role=button[name="Save"]'. |
| `text` | string | yes | - | Text to put in the field. Replaces the current value. |
| `submit` | boolean | no | `false` | Press Enter afterwards (submits most forms). |
| `timeout_s` | number (> 0) | no | `15.0` | Seconds to wait before failing; capped at the server maximum. |

Returns structured output (`structuredContent`) as well as text.

### `browser_wait`

Wait for exactly one condition: a visible selector, visible text, a URL glob, or a load state
('networkidle' waits for 500ms without requests). Fails on timeout.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page_id` | string | yes | - | Page id returned by browser_open (e.g. 'p1'). |
| `selector` | string or null | no | `null` | Wait until an element matching this is visible. |
| `text` | string or null | no | `null` | Wait until this text is visible on the page. |
| `url_pattern` | string or null | no | `null` | Wait until the page URL matches this glob, e.g. '**/dashboard'. |
| `load_state` | one of `load`, `domcontentloaded`, `networkidle` or null | no | `null` | Wait for this load state. |
| `timeout_s` | number (> 0) | no | `15.0` | Seconds to wait before failing; capped at the server maximum. |

Returns structured output (`structuredContent`) as well as text.
